proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\) and fixed known constants \(C_\theta,C_g,C_q>0\).  For each \(N\), let \(\widehat g_N\) and \(\widehat q_N\) be fixed measurable functions on the covariate domain satisfying \(\lvert\widehat g_N\rvert\le C_g\) and \(\lvert\widehat q_N\rvert\le C_q\) pointwise, and let \(a_N,b_N>0\), with \(a_N<1\) eventually.  Define \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{JMS}}_{N,8}(a_N,b_N;\widehat g_N,\widehat q_N)\) to be the full uncertainty class of one-observation laws \(R\) of \(Z=(X,T,Y)\) in the partially linear model
\[
 Y=\vartheta(R)T+f_R(X)+\xi_R,
 \qquad E_R[\xi_R\mid X,T]=0,
 \qquad
 T=g_R(X)+\eta_R,
 \qquad \eta_R\mid X\sim\mathcal N(0,1),
\]
such that
\[
 \lvert\vartheta(R)\rvert\le C_\theta,
 \qquad \lvert g_R(X)\rvert\le C_g\quad R\text{-almost surely},
 \qquad \lvert Y\rvert\le C_q\quad R\text{-almost surely},
\]
and, writing \(q_R(x)=E_R[Y\mid X=x]\) and \(R_X\) for the covariate marginal,
\[
 \lVert\widehat g_N-g_R\rVert_{L^8(R_X)}\le a_N,
 \qquad
 \lVert\widehat q_N-q_R\rVert_{L^8(R_X)}\le b_N.
\]
This is the specialization to \(\sigma=1\) and \(s=8\) of the full class \(\mathcal P_{s,\epsilon}(\widehat h;\Phi^\star)\) in Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis, Theorem 3.2.  If
\[
 a_Nb_N=o\!\left((\log N)^{-1/2}\right),
 \qquad
 \Lambda_N^{\mathrm{JMS}}
 =\left\{\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right\}^{3},
\]
then, for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\vartheta_N}
 \sup_{R\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{JMS}}_{N,8}(a_N,b_N;\widehat g_N,\widehat q_N)}
 Q_{R^{\otimes N},1-\gamma}\!\left(
   \left\lvert\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta(R)\right\rvert
 \right)
 \ge c_\gamma\left{
 N^{-1/2}+a_Nb_N\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{JMS}}
 \right},
\]
where the infimum is over all measurable estimators based on \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}R\), \(Q_{R^{\otimes N},u}(V)=\inf\{t:R^{\otimes N}(V\le t)\ge u\}\), and \(c_\gamma>0\) depends only on \(\gamma\).  In the cited proof, Appendix D equation (56) supplies only the term \(a_Nb_N\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) through the moment-matched fuzzy construction.  The Gaussian two-point model in equation (57) and its conclusion (58) separately supply the term \(N^{-1/2}\); the theorem combines these two lower bounds and does not assert that a single fuzzy-support witness supplies their sum.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current last sentence inaccurately attributes the entire sum to the moment-matched fuzzy hypotheses. Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis, Theorem 3.2 and equation (6), give the full-class minimax bound, but Appendix D equation (56) proves only the nuisance-product/logarithmic term, while equations (57)--(58) prove the separate parametric term. The replacement also specializes the source theorem to the needed case \(\sigma=1\), \(s=8\), and states the source class, supplied-fit bounds, nuisance radii, sampling law, and uniformity explicitly.

prose_updates.tldr: For a primitive JMS partially linear law and fixed training-realized nuisance fits supplied within stated \(L^8(P_X)\) radii, one interval is honest over exact-Gaussian and shrinking fourth-cumulant-separated branches of the projected evaluation experiment. Four explicit Bonferroni-calibrated median-of-means events use nonempty finite-sample block partitions and cover safe DML, four residual moments, centered Appell inversion, and its empirical slope. The non-Gaussian finite-sample length is \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n+d_np_{\mathrm{sel},n}\}\), with an explicit bound on \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\), and reduces to \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n\}\) when \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\). For bounded supplied-fit sequences satisfying the published pointwise fit bounds and nuisance-product condition, direct inclusion of the full Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Gaussian class yields the certified Gaussian coordinate \(d_n^-=n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\); it needs neither conditional-transfer axioms nor an auxiliary outcome-variance subclass. A common-fit branch selector rules out the bounded-chi-square cross-branch fuzzy route at strong separation. The logarithm in \(\Lambda_n\), the within-non-Gaussian lower face, and hence a matching Pareto frontier remain open, and no improvement of global union-supremum expected length is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Published structure-agnostic partially linear model theory and the sibling repository paper study separate Gaussian or fixed-non-Gaussian point-estimation classes and fixed-separation spectral constructions, not one conditionally specified projected experiment with union honesty, shrinking cumulant separation, and branchwise expected length. Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis do supply the exact full-class Gaussian minimax benchmark, including its retained logarithmic factor, but not the local-to-Gaussian union-honest frontier.
project_justification.niche: The informative object is the two-coordinate expected-length region. The global union supremum remains governed by the Gaussian coordinate, while fixed positive-weight scalarizations are rate-degenerate and do not encode branchwise adaptation.
project_justification.fill: The proved upper component combines explicit nonempty-block four-event calibration, a finite-sample branch-selection error envelope, a safe unnormalized DML interval, and a fully centered split Appell inversion. On bounded supplied-fit sequences obeying the source bounds and product condition, a direct inclusion of the full Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis class into the present Gaussian branch, followed by the interval-length reduction, proves \(L_G(C_n)\gtrsim n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\). This transfer fixes interior constants inside the present envelope and uses upward closure from the included subclass; it does not assume support-by-support transfer, conditional outcome-variance nondegeneracy, or a fit-dependent oracle family. The selector impossibility theorem closes the bounded-chi-square cross-branch fuzzy route at strong separation, while the within-non-Gaussian lower face and removal of \(\Lambda_n\) remain open.

prose_updates.related_work: Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis, Theorem 3.2, give the full-class Gaussian-treatment minimax lower scale \(N^{-1/2}+a_Nb_N\{\log(1/a_N)/\log N\}^3\) for bounded supplied fits. Their Appendix D equation (56) derives only the nuisance-product/logarithmic term from moment-matched fuzzy hypotheses; their Gaussian model (57) and conclusion (58) separately derive the parametric term. The present Gaussian-coordinate theorem transfers that published theorem by direct inclusion of an interior fixed-constant subclass, rather than by postulating compatibility of particular fuzzy supports. Their Theorem 5.4 informs the fixed-separation ACE component but does not give a union-honest shrinking-cumulant interval. Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik, Theorems 5 and 8--10, inform the Gaussian obstruction and higher-order score. Cai and Low, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, inform branchwise expected length, while their Gaussian model has no learned partially linear residual; their 2011 Hermite mixture method informs the fuzzy-prior handle. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman inform localized product-mixture calculations. Chernozhukov et al. supply the split DML benchmark. Zheng, Bonvini, and Guo's Theorem 2 informs filtered-union coverage and interval-length control, while their Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient; neither theorem uses treatment cumulants. The sibling repository paper \(\texttt{stat\_sa\_plm\_cumulant\_converse}\) proves fixed-separation spectral and estimation constructions and explicitly leaves shrinking separation, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and a local matching lower bound unresolved. The present proved contribution is the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier together with the direct-inclusion Gaussian coordinate at \(d_n^-\); it does not claim a matching Pareto frontier. Quessy and Mailhot analyze centered and studentized normality statistics without nuisance-contaminated residuals. Armstrong, Kline, and Sun motivate caution about pretesting for a different point-risk object.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-=n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\), not \(d_n\) in regimes where \(\Lambda_n\) vanishes. Its direct published-class inclusion applies to bounded supplied-fit sequences satisfying the source pointwise bounds and product smallness condition, after fixing interior constants compatible with the stated universal lower threshold on \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\); it does not cover arbitrary unbounded external fits. The source's full minimax theorem combines two different mechanisms: equation (56) gives only the fuzzy nuisance-product/logarithmic term, and equations (57)--(58) give the separate parametric term. The upper theorem does not need the lower-subclass fit bounds and does not identify a matching Pareto boundary. Its finite-sample guarantee starts at \(n=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), when every requested calibration block count is available. The early bounded-chi-square cross-branch Rademacher/Hermite route is resolved negatively at strong separation because the common-fit selector makes the mixtures asymptotically singular; a within-non-Gaussian or constrained-risk experiment is still required for the actual lower frontier.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The law class is primitive and contains no learner-performance condition. All upper-frontier inference is conditional on fixed supplied fits and uniform over their radius set. The Appell polynomial estimates the first four raw residual moments on a fold independent of inversion. Every median-of-means operator partitions the sample into \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty blocks, and the upper theorem assumes \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\). Four named events receive error \(\alpha/4\) each, while the separate bound \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\) quantifies wrong-branch selection. The Gaussian lower theorem takes \(N=3n\), fixes source constants strictly inside the present envelope once \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\) exceeds the stated universal feasibility threshold, and includes the full \(s=8\), \(\sigma=1\) Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis class for every bounded supplied-fit sequence satisfying their pointwise fit bounds and nuisance-product condition. Constant conditional \(\mathcal N(0,1)\) treatment noise is independent of \(X\) and has unit variance; the source partially linear laws impose \(E[\xi\mid X,T]=0\); and bounded \(Y\), \(q_0\), \(\theta_0\), and \(g_0\), together with Gaussian \(\eta\), give the required unconditional sub-Gaussian envelope after the fixed constants are chosen. The source \(L^8\) balls are exactly the present supplied-fit set, so upward transfer and the interval-length reduction yield the Gaussian coordinate. No support-localization axiom, auxiliary conditional outcome-variance condition, or nondegenerate Gaussian subclass is used. The sibling repository paper settles fixed-separation spectral estimation, not this local-to-Gaussian union-honest length problem. The within-non-Gaussian converse and removal of \(\Lambda_n\) are open. No matching Pareto boundary or improvement of global union-supremum expected length is claimed.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(N=3n\), and let \(\mathfrak J_n\) be the JMS uncertainty class in \(\textup{lem:jms-gaussian-class-inclusion}\).  By \(\textup{def:projected-experiment}\), concatenating \(D_K,D_D,D_A\) identifies \(Q_P\) with \(P^{\otimes N}\).  Thus an interval measurable in the three folds is an interval in the \(N\)-observation experiment.

Fix \(\gamma=3/4\); because \(\alpha<1/2\), one has \(\gamma>\alpha\).  Define the source logarithmic factor
\[
 \Lambda_{N,n}=
 \begin{cases}
  1, & \varepsilon_{g,n}=0,\\
  \displaystyle
  \min\!\left\{1,
  \left[\frac{1\vee\log(1/\varepsilon_{g,n})}{\log(eN)}\right]^3
  \right\}, & \varepsilon_{g,n}>0,
 \end{cases}
\]
and put
\[
 R_n=N^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_{N,n}.
\]
The product-smallness hypothesis is exactly the one needed by \(\textup{lem:jms-gaussian-fuzzy-benchmark}\) at sample size \(N\), with treatment-noise variance one, power \(s=8\), the fixed bounds chosen in \(\textup{lem:jms-gaussian-class-inclusion}\), and supplied center \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\).  The cited full-class theorem therefore supplies a constant \(c_0>0\) such that
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\theta}
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak J_n}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(
 |\widehat\theta-\theta_0(P)|
 \right)
 \geq c_0R_n
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Here the infimum is over all estimators based on the \(N\) observations.  This invocation uses the theorem-level sum.  As recorded in the cited node, its Appendix D equation (56) supplies only the nuisance-product logarithmic term, while equations (57)--(58) supply the separate parametric term; no single fuzzy-support witness is claimed to supply their sum.

Let \(\widehat\theta\) be arbitrary and set \(r_n=c_0R_n/2\).  The preceding minimax inequality implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak J_n}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(
 |\widehat\theta-\theta_0(P)|
 \right)\geq c_0R_n.
\]
By the definition of a supremum, some \(P\in\mathfrak J_n\) has the displayed quantile strictly larger than \(r_n\).  By the definition
\(Q_{P,u}(V)=\inf\{t:P(V\leq t)\geq u\}\), this entails
\[
 P^{\otimes N}\{ |\widehat\theta-\theta_0(P)|>r_n\}>\gamma.
\]
Thus the hypothesis of \(\textup{lem:honest-interval-length-reduction}\) holds for the \(N\)-observation laws \(\{P^{\otimes N}:P\in\mathfrak J_n\}\), with radius \(r_n\) and error probability \(\beta=\gamma\).

By \(\textup{lem:jms-gaussian-class-inclusion}\), every \(P\in\mathfrak J_n\) lies in \(\mathcal G_n\) and satisfies \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\).  By \(\textup{def:honesty-union}\), \(\mathcal G_n\subseteq\mathcal U_n\); hence the assumed union honesty of \(C_n\) implies
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathfrak J_n}Q_P\{\theta_0(P)\in C_n\}
 \geq1-\alpha.
\]
Applying \(\textup{lem:honest-interval-length-reduction}\) and using \(Q_P=P^{\otimes N}\) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak J_n}E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \geq2r_n(\gamma-\alpha)
 =c_0(\gamma-\alpha)R_n.
\]

It remains only to compare the sample-size conventions.  Since \(N=3n\),
\[
 N^{-1/2}=3^{-1/2}n^{-1/2}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \log(eN)=\log(3en)
 \leq(1+\log3)\log(en).
\]
For every \(x\geq0\) and \(a\geq1\),
\(\min\{1,x/a\}\geq a^{-1}\min\{1,x\}\).  Applying this with the cubed logarithmic ratios, and treating \(\varepsilon_{g,n}=0\) by the first branch of the definition, yields
\[
 \Lambda_{N,n}\geq(1+\log3)^{-3}\Lambda_n.
\]
Consequently, for a universal \(c_1>0\),
\[
 R_n
 \geq c_1\left\{n^{-1/2}
 +\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\right\}
 =c_1d_n^-
\]
by \(\textup{def:rate-scales}\).  Finally, the inclusion of \(\mathfrak J_n\) and \(\textup{def:length-vector}\) imply
\[
 L_G(C_n)
 =\sup_{P\in\mathcal G_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \geq \sup_{P\in\mathfrak J_n}E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \geq c d_n^-,
\]
where \(c=c_0(\gamma-\alpha)c_1>0\).  The argument uses neither \(\textup{ass:outcome-noise-variance}\) nor \(\textup{def:gaussian-nondegenerate-subclass}\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\nu_G=\sqrt{8/3}\), suppose \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\geq \nu_G\), and put \(b=C_{\mathrm{env}}/16\).  Set \(N=3n\), and suppose
\[
 \max\{\|\widehat g\|_\infty,\|\widehat q\|_\infty\}\leq b.
\]
Let \(\mathfrak J_n\) be the uncertainty class in \(\textup{lem:jms-gaussian-fuzzy-benchmark}\) instantiated at sample size \(N\), treatment-noise standard deviation one, power \(s=8\), with each of the fixed bounds on \(|\theta_0|\), \(|g_0(X)|\), and \(|Y|\) equal to \(b\), supplied center \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\), and nuisance radii \((\varepsilon_{g,n},\varepsilon_{q,n})\).  Thus its base laws are the source partially linear laws satisfying \(\eta\mid X\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\) and those three bounds, and its uncertainty restriction is exactly
\[
 \|\widehat g-g_0\|_{L^8(P_X)}\leq\varepsilon_{g,n},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat q-q_0\|_{L^8(P_X)}\leq\varepsilon_{q,n}.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathfrak J_n\subseteq
 \{P\in\mathcal G_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak J_n\).  By the definition of the JMS base class recorded in \(\textup{lem:jms-gaussian-fuzzy-benchmark}\), its variables satisfy the partially linear equations
\[
 Y=\theta_0T+f_0(X)+\xi,
 \qquad
 T=g_0(X)+\eta,
\]
with \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\), and the conditional law of \(\eta\) given \(X\) is \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).  These give \(\textup{ass:outcome-equation}\), \(\textup{ass:treatment-equation}\), and \(\textup{ass:outcome-orthogonality}\).

The conditional Gaussian law is constant in \(X\).  Thus, for Borel sets \(A\subseteq\mathbb R\) and measurable sets \(B\subseteq\mathcal X\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P\{\eta\in A,X\in B\}
 &=E_P\!\left[\mathbf 1_{\{X\in B\}}
      P\{\eta\in A\mid X\}\right] \\
 &=\Phi(A)P_X(B),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the standard normal law.  Hence \(\eta\perp X\), proving \(\textup{ass:independent-treatment-noise}\), and Gaussian integration gives \(E_P[\eta^2]=1\), proving \(\textup{ass:unit-treatment-variance}\).

It remains to verify the envelope.  The source bounds imply
\[
 |\theta_0|\leq b,
 \qquad |g_0(X)|\leq b,
 \qquad |Y|\leq b
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Because \(q_0(X)=E_P[Y\mid X]\), conditional Jensen gives \(|q_0(X)|\leq b\) almost surely.  Iterated conditional expectation and the two partially linear equations give
\[
 q_0(X)=\theta_0g_0(X)+f_0(X),
 \qquad
 \xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0\eta.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 |\xi|\leq 2b+b|\eta|,
 \qquad
 \frac{\xi^2}{C_{\mathrm{env}}^2}
 \leq \frac1{32}+\frac{\eta^2}{128}.
\]
For a standard normal variable, direct integration yields
\[
 E_P\exp(\eta^2/c^2)=(1-2/c^2)^{-1/2}
 \quad(c^2>2).
\]
In particular, the defining Luxemburg inequality for the sub-Gaussian norm is an equality at \(c^2=8/3\), so \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}=\nu_G\leq C_{\mathrm{env}}\).  The preceding pointwise inequality also gives
\[
 E_P\exp\!\left(\frac{\xi^2}{C_{\mathrm{env}}^2}\right)
 \leq e^{1/32}(1-1/64)^{-1/2}<2.
\]
For completeness, the last strict inequality follows after taking logarithms from \(-\log(1-x)\leq2x\) at \(x=1/64\), because the logarithm of the left side is at most \(3/64<\log 2\).  Therefore \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2}\leq C_{\mathrm{env}}\).  Since \(b<C_{\mathrm{env}}\), all components of \(\textup{ass:uniform-envelope}\) hold.  By \(\textup{def:jms-law-class}\), \(P\in\mathcal P_n\); the marginal law \(\eta\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\) and \(\textup{def:gaussian-branch}\) then give \(P\in\mathcal G_n\).

Finally, the \(s=8\) uncertainty restriction defining \(\mathfrak J_n\) is
\[
 \|\widehat g-g_0\|_{L^8(P_X)}\leq\varepsilon_{g,n},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat q-q_0\|_{L^8(P_X)}\leq\varepsilon_{q,n}.
\]
These are exactly the two inequalities in \(\textup{def:supplied-fit-set}\), so \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\).  Both asserted memberships follow.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(\nu_G=\sqrt{8/3}\), suppose \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\geq\nu_G\), put \(b=C_{\mathrm{env}}/16\), and set \(N=3n\).  Fix a deterministic sequence of supplied pairs satisfying
\[
 \max\{\|\widehat g\|_\infty,\|\widehat q\|_\infty\}\leq b,
\]
and suppose, along the indices for which \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}>0\), that
\[
 \varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}
 =o\!\left((\log N)^{-1/2}\right).
\]
Then there is a constant \(c>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), every evaluation-measurable interval \(C_n\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal U_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 Q_P\{\theta_0\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha
\]
obeys
\[
 L_G(C_n)\geq c d_n^-.
\]
This is a Gaussian-coordinate lower bound only.  It retains \(\Lambda_n\), imposes no conditional outcome-variance restriction, and makes no assertion of a matching Pareto frontier or of an improved global union-supremum length.
